In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
common genetic variants in TRPM6 are unlikely to play a major role in the pathogenesis of type 2 diabetes, but they might be involved in the pathogenesis under certain environmental circumstances.
common TRPM6 variants do not appear to be a major risk factor for diabetes in women.
the results from the current study do not provide evidence of an association between common genetic variants of TRPM6 and risk of type II diabetes in women.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

common variants of TRPM6 and magnesium intake are not robustly associated with type 2 diabetes, but the rare haplotype of two non-synonymous SNPs of TRPM6 (Ile1393Val-Lys1584Gle) is significantly associated with increased diabetes risk in women who have lower magnesium intake.
common genetic variants of TRPM6 and/or TRPM7 may contribute to the development of diabetes only in the presence of low magnesium intake.
TRPM6 and/or TRPM7 may play a role in the pathogenesis of type 2 Diabetes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the common TRPM6 coding variants may modify the risk of type 1 and type 2 diabetes, and that magnesium intake may modify the risk associated with the rare allele of these variants.
magnesium may be an important nutrient for diabetes prevention, particularly among people with certain genotypes of TRPM6 and magnesium intake.
the TRPM6 Ile1393-Val1584 haplotype is associated with an increased risk of diabetes in women who have low magnesium intake.
